en.name: Pine nuts
en.summary: Pine nuts keep 2–3 weeks in the cupboard, 3 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 9 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). They are the most expensive nut in most kitchens and one of the quickest to turn, which is a bad combination worth planning around.
en.pantry: 2–3 weeks in a sealed, opaque container somewhere cool and dark. Pine nuts are small, soft and very high in unsaturated fat, so there is a lot of oil meeting air across a lot of surface. Nothing grows in them; they oxidise, and they do it faster than almost any other nut on the shelf. Given what they cost, treat the cupboard as a place for the portion you are cooking with this week and put the rest away cold.
en.fridge: 3 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, sealed tight. Refrigeration genuinely extends pine nuts rather than merely holding them, because the enemy is oxidation and cold slows the reaction down. Keep them away from onions and anything smoked — pine nuts are mild and oily and absorb odours quickly. Toast them only as you use them; a toasted nut goes rancid faster than a raw one.
en.freezer: 9 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Store them in a plastic bag inside an airtight container — two barriers, because the fat is fragile enough that a single thin bag lets in too much air over months. There is very little water in a pine nut, so the texture is unaffected and they toast straight from frozen.
en.thawing: No thawing needed; use them from frozen. Let the sealed container reach room temperature before opening if you have taken the whole lot out.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp taste — the classic sign, and one nut is enough.
A smell of old cooking oil or paint rather than resin and butter.
Nuts that have gone soft and chewy instead of snapping cleanly.
Yellowing or dark spots on nuts that should be pale ivory.
tips: Buy small quantities often rather than a big bag once.
Keep the working handful out and the rest in the freezer.
Toast just before use, and toast gently; they burn in seconds.
Taste one before adding them to a pesto — rancid pine nuts ruin the whole batch.

faq.q: How long do pine nuts keep?
faq.a: 2–3 weeks in the cupboard, 3 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 9 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Should pine nuts be kept in the fridge or freezer?
faq.a: Yes, for anything you are not using within a couple of weeks. They are among the fastest nuts to go rancid, and cold storage multiplies their life several times over.

faq.q: How can you tell if pine nuts have gone bad?
faq.a: Taste one. Rancid pine nuts are sharply bitter, and the bitterness survives toasting and carries straight into a pesto or a salad.

zh.name: 松子
zh.summary: 松子放櫥櫃可放 2～3 週，4 °C 以下冷藏 3 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 9 個月。它大概是多數廚房裡最貴的堅果，同時也是走味最快的其中之一——這個組合值得先做打算。
zh.pantry: 密封、不透光的容器，放陰涼避光處，2～3 週。松子小、軟，不飽和脂肪比例很高，等於很多油以很大的表面積接觸空氣。它不是長出東西，而是在氧化，而且速度比架上幾乎所有堅果都快。考慮到它的價格，櫥櫃只適合放這週要用的那一份，其餘請低溫收好。
zh.fridge: 確實密封放 4 °C 以下，3 個月。冷藏對松子來說是真的在延長，而不只是拖著，因為敵人是氧化，低溫會把反應速度壓下來。請遠離洋蔥和任何燻製品——松子味淡油多，吸味很快。要用時才烘香；烘過的松子比生的更快油耗。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 9 個月。請把松子裝進塑膠袋、再放進氣密容器——兩層屏障，因為它的油脂脆弱到只用一層薄袋子，幾個月下來進的空氣就太多了。松子含水極少，質地不受影響，可以直接從冷凍拿出來烘。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍，直接從冷凍用。整包拿出來的話，請讓密封容器回到室溫再打開。
spoilage: 嚐起來苦而尖銳——最經典的訊號，一顆就夠。
聞起來像久放的油或油漆，而不是松脂與奶香。
松子變軟變韌，咬下去不再清脆。
本該是米白色的松子出現泛黃或深色斑點。
tips: 少量多次買，不要一次買一大包。
近期要用的放外面，其餘全部冷凍。
用之前才烘，而且火要小，它幾秒鐘就會焦。
做青醬前先吃一顆；油耗的松子會毀掉一整罐。

faq.a: 放櫥櫃 2～3 週，4 °C 以下冷藏 3 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 9 個月。

faq.q: 松子要放冷藏還是冷凍？
faq.a: 兩週內用不完的話都該低溫保存。它是走味最快的堅果之一，冷藏冷凍能把壽命拉長好幾倍。
吃一顆。油耗的松子苦得很明顯，而且這個苦味烘過也不會消失，會整個進到青醬或沙拉裡。
